key_insight: In epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, optical and Hall measurements give matching mobilities, showing that intrinsic charge transport can persist over millimetre scales without being dominated by static disorder.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical benchmark and measurement protocol for designing and validating high-quality perovskite semiconductors for optoelectronic devices.
method: Concurrent optical pump-terahertz probe (OPTP) and Hall-effect measurements on the same single-crystal sample
Temperature-dependent mobility tracking to compare ultrafast/local and macroscopic transport
Use of epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals to minimize defects and extrinsic disorder
evidence_signal: Both techniques report consistent room-temperature hole mobilities of about 30 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and similar band-like temperature exponents, indicating the same intrinsic transport mechanism.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated on high-quality epitaxial single crystals, so performance may be harder to reproduce in polycrystalline films or defect-rich device stacks.
paper_title: Matching Terahertz and Hall Mobilities as a Hallmark of Intrinsic Charge Transport in Metal-Halide Perovskites
